tfng.p: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support roughly a quarter of all marine species. Reefs also protect coastlines by absorbing the energy of waves, and millions of people depend on them for food. Rising sea temperatures cause corals to expel the algae that feed them, a process known as bleaching. Some scientists believe that bleached reefs can recover if the water cools quickly enough, although the evidence so far is limited.
q: Coral reefs occupy about a quarter of the ocean floor.
FALSE
Matn: ‘less than one percent of the ocean floor’. ‘A quarter’ — bu ular qo‘llab-quvvatlaydigan turlar ulushi, maydon emas.
Reefs reduce the force of waves that reach the shore.
TRUE
‘protect coastlines by absorbing the energy of waves’ = to‘lqin kuchini kamaytiradi (paraphrase).
Bleaching occurs when corals produce too much algae.
FALSE
Matn aksini aytadi: corals ‘expel the algae’ — ya’ni suvo‘tlarni chiqarib yuboradi.
Most governments have introduced laws to protect coral reefs.
NOT GIVEN
Matnda hukumatlar yoki qonunlar haqida hech narsa yo‘q — NOT GIVEN.

tfng.p: Several companies have recently tested a four-day working week with no reduction in pay. In one trial involving over sixty firms, most employees reported lower stress and better sleep. Managers noted that meetings became shorter, and productivity stayed roughly the same. However, a number of employers in the retail sector found it difficult to arrange shifts, and a few returned to a five-day pattern after the trial ended.
q: Employees in the trial were paid less for working fewer days.
FALSE
‘with no reduction in pay’ — maosh kamaymagan.
Most employees in the trial said they felt less stressed.
TRUE
‘most employees reported lower stress’ = ko‘pchilik stress kamayganini aytgan.
Productivity increased significantly during the trial.
FALSE
‘productivity stayed roughly the same’ — oshmagan, taxminan bir xil.
Retail employers were the most enthusiastic about the change.
NOT GIVEN
Retail kompaniyalar qiyinchilikka duch kelgani aytilgan, lekin ‘eng ishtiyoqli’ ekani haqida ma’lumot yo‘q.

tfng.p: Before the fifteenth century, books in Europe were copied by hand, which made them expensive and rare. Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, introduced around 1450, allowed texts to be produced far more quickly. Within fifty years, millions of books had been printed across the continent. Historians generally agree that the press helped ideas spread faster, though they disagree about how much it contributed to the religious reforms of the sixteenth century.
q: Hand-copied books were costly in medieval Europe.
TRUE
‘copied by hand, which made them expensive’.
Gutenberg invented the first printing technology in the world.
NOT GIVEN
Matn faqat Yevropa va Gutenberg haqida; ‘dunyodagi birinchi’ deyilmagan.
Historians are unanimous about the press’s role in religious reform.
FALSE
‘they disagree about how much it contributed’ — fikrlar bir xil emas.
Printed books were widespread in Europe by around 1500.
TRUE
1450 dan ‘within fifty years, millions of books had been printed’ = taxminan 1500 gacha.

tfng.p: In recent years, keeping bees on city rooftops has become popular in many capitals. City bees often produce more honey than their countryside relatives, partly because gardens and parks offer a wider variety of flowers throughout the year. Some experts worry, however, that too many urban hives may compete with wild pollinators for limited food. A study in one large city found no evidence of pollution in the honey, but researchers say further testing is needed.
q: Urban bees sometimes make more honey than rural bees.
TRUE
‘often produce more honey than their countryside relatives’.
Parks and gardens flower only during the summer months.
FALSE
‘variety of flowers throughout the year’ — yil davomida.
The honey in the study was found to contain pollution.
FALSE
‘found no evidence of pollution’ — ifloslanish topilmagan.
Rooftop beekeeping is more profitable than keeping bees in the countryside.
NOT GIVEN
Asal ko‘pligi haqida gap bor, lekin foyda (profit) haqida hech narsa yo‘q.

tfng.p: Researchers have long suspected that sleep plays a role in memory. In a well-known experiment, students who slept after learning a list of words remembered about twenty percent more than those who stayed awake for the same period. Brain scans suggest that during deep sleep the brain replays recent experiences, strengthening the connections between neurons. It remains unclear whether short daytime naps have the same effect.
q: Students who slept after studying recalled more words than those who did not.
TRUE
‘remembered about twenty percent more’.
Deep sleep is the only stage in which the brain strengthens memories.
NOT GIVEN
Faqat deep sleep haqida gap ketgan; ‘yagona bosqich’ deb aytilmagan.
Scientists have proved that short naps improve memory.
FALSE
‘It remains unclear’ — noaniq, isbotlanmagan.
The experiment involved the same list of words for every student.
NOT GIVEN
Bir xil ro‘yxat ekani aytilmagan (‘a list of words’ — umumiy).

tfng.p: Microplastics are tiny fragments, usually smaller than five millimetres, that result from the breakdown of larger plastic items. They have been found in oceans, rivers, and even in drinking water. A large proportion of the fragments in the sea come from synthetic clothing, which sheds fibres during washing. Although the health effects on humans are not yet fully understood, several countries have banned microbeads in cosmetic products.
q: Microplastics are defined as fragments under five millimetres in size.
TRUE
‘usually smaller than five millimetres’.
Most microplastics in the sea originate from plastic bags.
FALSE
Asosiy manba — synthetic clothing (kiyim), bag emas.
Microplastics have been confirmed to cause illness in humans.
FALSE
‘health effects ... not yet fully understood’ — tasdiqlanmagan.
Microbeads are banned in cosmetics in every country.
FALSE
‘several countries’ — ba’zi mamlakatlar, har bir emas.

tfng.p: Sales of electric vehicles have grown rapidly, helped by government subsidies and falling battery prices. Critics point out that manufacturing a battery produces more carbon dioxide than building a petrol car, but studies show that this difference is usually offset within two years of driving. A remaining challenge is the availability of charging points, which are still scarce in rural areas.
q: Government support has contributed to the growth in electric vehicle sales.
TRUE
‘helped by government subsidies’.
Making an electric car battery causes less pollution than building a petrol car.
FALSE
Aksincha: batareya ishlab chiqarish ko‘proq CO2 chiqaradi.
The extra carbon cost of an electric car is usually recovered within two years.
TRUE
‘offset within two years of driving’.
Charging points are more common in rural areas than in cities.
FALSE
Rural areas’da ‘still scarce’ — kam.

tfng.p: Around ten percent of people are left-handed, a proportion that has remained fairly stable across cultures and centuries. Studies of ancient tools and cave paintings suggest that left-handers existed in prehistoric times. Some researchers claim that left-handed people are more creative, but a large survey found no clear difference. Left-handers were once forced to write with their right hand in many schools.
q: The proportion of left-handed people has varied greatly over time.
FALSE
‘remained fairly stable’ — barqaror.
Evidence suggests left-handed people lived in prehistoric times.
TRUE
‘ancient tools and cave paintings suggest ... existed in prehistoric times’.
A large survey proved that left-handers are more creative.
FALSE
‘found no clear difference’.
Left-handed pupils today receive special support in most schools.
NOT GIVEN
Hozirgi maktablar haqida ma’lumot yo‘q (faqat ‘once forced’).

paras: A

Planting trees along streets reduces the temperature of a city by providing shade and releasing moisture. In some districts, summer readings were up to five degrees lower in tree-lined areas than on bare roads.
B
Beyond cooling, trees absorb dust and gases produced by traffic. Residents of green neighbourhoods report fewer breathing problems, although researchers admit that income levels also play a role.
C
Maintaining urban trees is costly. Roots can damage pavements and pipes, and fallen leaves must be cleared. Several councils have therefore chosen smaller species that need less space.
D
Public attitudes are changing. Early plans rarely included green space, but surveys now show that most citizens would pay slightly higher taxes for more parks.
h: A natural way of lowering heat

w.A: A: shade va namlik — harorat pasayishi (‘lowering heat’). ‘cooling’ bosh g‘oya.
w.B: B: chang va gazlarni yutadi, nafas muammolari kam — ‘Cleaner air and better health’.
w.C: C: xarajat, ildizlar quvur/yo‘lni buzadi — ‘financial and practical drawbacks’.
w.D: D: ‘attitudes are changing’ = ommaviy fikr o‘zgarishi. vi (history) bo‘lmaydi — faqat bitta jumla tarixga tegadi.

paras: A
Children seem to pick up languages effortlessly, but adults can succeed too. Studies show that adults learn grammar rules faster, while children achieve more natural pronunciation.
B
Immersion programmes place learners in an environment where only the target language is spoken. Participants often make rapid progress, mainly because they are forced to communicate every day.
C
Technology has introduced new tools, from translation apps to online tutors. Yet some teachers fear that constant reliance on apps discourages students from thinking for themselves.
D

Motivation is considered the strongest predictor of success. Learners who have a personal reason to study — a job, a partner, a move abroad — tend to persist longer than those who study only for a grade.
h: Why the young have an advantage
The importance of personal reasons to study

w.A: A: kattalar grammatikada, bolalar talaffuzda kuchli — ‘Comparing adult and child learners’ (ii emas: yoshlar ustunligi bir tomonlama).
w.B: B: faqat target til muhitida — ‘total exposure’.
w.C: C: ilovalarga haddan tashqari tayanish xavfi — ‘dependence on devices’.
w.D: D: motivation, shaxsiy sabab — ‘personal reasons to study’.

paras: A
Glass can be recycled endlessly without losing quality. Crushed glass, called cullet, melts at a lower temperature than raw materials, so factories save energy by using it.
B
Despite this, many countries recycle less than half of their glass. A common problem is contamination: ceramics and heat-resistant glass mixed into bottle banks can ruin an entire batch.
C
Some nations have achieved recycling rates above ninety percent through deposit schemes, in which shoppers pay a small fee on each bottle and receive it back on return.
D
Researchers are now exploring new uses for waste glass, such as road surfacing and building insulation, to create demand for material that cannot be remade into bottles.
h: A system that rewards returning bottles
New factories planned for coastal areas

w.A: A: cheksiz qayta ishlanadi, energiya tejaydi — ‘unusually efficient material’.
w.B: B: ‘many countries recycle less than half’ + contamination — nega past.
w.D: D: yo‘l qoplamasi, izolyatsiya — ishlatib bo‘lmaydigan material uchun yangi yo‘nalishlar.

maps.script: Welcome to the Riverside Community Centre. We are standing at the main entrance, at the bottom of the plan. The corridor runs left and right in front of us. Right next to the entrance, on the left, is the cafe, which opens at eight o'clock. Beyond the cafe, at the far left end, you will find the changing rooms. On the right of the entrance there is the gym, and at the far right end of the bottom row is the storeroom, which is for staff only. Now, across the corridor, on the top row. The library is directly opposite the cafe. The computer room is next to the library, on its right. The art studio is at the far left of the top row, above the changing rooms. And finally, the meeting room is on the top row, next to the lift.

q.why: ‘Right next to the entrance, on the left, is the cafe’ — kirishning chap yonida: F.
‘Beyond the cafe, at the far left end’ — eng chap chekka: E.
‘On the right of the entrance there is the gym’ — kirishning o‘ng yonida: G.
‘directly opposite the cafe’ — kafening qarshisida (yuqori qator): B.
‘next to the library, on its right’ — kutubxonaning o‘ng tomonida: C.
‘on the top row, next to the lift’ — lift yonida: D.

maps.script: Let me explain the park layout. You enter on the left and follow the main path east towards the cafe, which is at the end of the path. On the left of the path, the building closest to the entrance is the reptile house. The aviary is the one in the middle. The gift shop is the last building on the left, just above the cafe. Now the right-hand side. The penguin pool is directly opposite the reptile house, and the otter enclosure is opposite the aviary. The children's farm is the building next to the cafe, opposite the gift shop.

q.why: ‘On the left ... closest to the entrance’: A.
‘the one in the middle’ (chap tomonda): B.
‘the last building on the left, just above the cafe’: C.
‘directly opposite the reptile house’ — A ning qarshisi: D.
‘opposite the aviary’ — B ning qarshisi: E.
‘next to the cafe, opposite the gift shop’: F.

maps.script: Welcome to Parkview Sports Complex. When you come in through the main entrance, you walk straight up the central corridor. The first door on the left, closest to the entrance, is the changing room. Next to it, further along on the same side, is the fitness suite. The squash courts are at the far end on the left. On the opposite side, the first door on the right is the physiotherapy room. The cafe is the next one along on the right, and the sports hall is right at the far end, on the right, facing the squash courts.

q.why: ‘first door on the left, closest to the entrance’: C.
‘Next to it, further along’ — keyingi eshik: B.
‘first door on the right’ (kirishga eng yaqin): F.
‘the next one along on the right’: E.
‘far end, on the right, facing the squash courts’: D.

para.s: The number of people living in cities has risen sharply.
m: There has been a dramatic increase in urban populations.

para.s: Many students find it difficult to concentrate in noisy places.
m: A large number of learners struggle to focus in loud environments.

para.s: Governments should spend more money on public transport.
m: Authorities ought to invest more in mass transit systems.

para.s: The use of mobile phones has changed the way people communicate.
m: Mobile devices have transformed how individuals interact with one another.

para.s: Young people are spending less time reading books than before.
m: Teenagers devote less of their time to books than in the past.

para.s: Pollution is a major problem in big cities.
m: Contamination of the environment is a serious issue in large urban areas.

para.s: Some people believe that children should start school at an early age.
m: It is argued by certain individuals that formal education ought to begin in early childhood.

para.s: The price of housing has increased dramatically in recent years.
m: Property costs have soared over the last few years.

para.s: Regular exercise has a positive effect on mental health.
m: Frequent physical activity benefits psychological well-being.

para.s: Online shopping is becoming more popular than visiting shops.
m: Buying goods over the internet is overtaking traditional in-store purchasing.

para.s: It is important to protect endangered species.
m: Safeguarding animals at risk of extinction is essential.

para.s: Working from home saves time and money for employees.
m: Remote working reduces both the time and the costs of staff.

para.s: Tourism can damage the local environment.
m: The travel industry may harm natural surroundings in a region.

para.s: Most people prefer to live near their families.
m: The majority of individuals would rather reside close to their relatives.

para.s: Technology makes it easier to learn a foreign language.
m: Digital tools simplify the process of acquiring another language.

para.s: The government introduced a new law to reduce traffic.
m: Legislation was brought in by the authorities to cut congestion.

col.q: It is not easy to ___ a decision when there are so many options.
col.n: make a decision — qaror qabul qilish

col.q: Students must ___ attention in class to understand the lesson.
The new policy will ___ a significant impact on small businesses.
col.n: have an impact on — ta’sir qilmoq

col.q: She decided to ___ a risk and start her own company.
Scientists ___ research to find a cure for the disease.
col.n: carry out / conduct research — tadqiqot o‘tkazmoq

col.q: Heavy rain can ___ serious damage to crops.
The government should ___ action to reduce pollution.
Parents play a ___ role in shaping a child’s character.
col.n: play a vital/key role — muhim rol o‘ynamoq

col.q: Many people ___ a living by working online.
col.n: make a living — pul topmoq/tirikchilik qilmoq

col.q: It is important to ___ a balance between work and leisure.
Climate change poses a serious ___ to the planet.
The company aims to ___ its carbon emissions by half.
Exercise can ___ stress and improve mood.
Some people ___ a strong case for banning cars in city centres.
col.n: make a case for — dalil keltirmoq

col.q: Pupils who ___ homework regularly usually perform better.
Many graduates struggle to ___ jobs in their chosen field.
col.n: find a job / secure a job — ish topmoq

col.q: Social media has become an integral ___ of modern life.
col.n: an integral part of — ajralmas qism

col.q: Governments need to ___ new laws to protect workers.
col.n: pass a law — qonun qabul qilmoq

col.q: The experiment ___ interesting results.
We must ___ the problem of unemployment seriously.
col.n: take a problem seriously — jiddiy qabul qilmoq

col.q: Students often face great ___ to succeed in exams.
A balanced diet is ___ to good health.
Rapid urbanisation has ___ to overcrowding.
The two countries ___ an agreement on trade last year.
Parents should ___ an example for their children.

tfng: Faqat matnga tayaning — o‘z bilimingiz bilan emas.
TRUE = matn bilan mos, FALSE = matn aksini aytadi, NOT GIVEN = matnda bu haqda ma’lumot yo‘q.
‘all/always/most/only’ kabi so‘zlarga e’tibor bering — ular ko‘pincha FALSE/NOT GIVEN ga olib boradi.
heads: Avval sarlavhalardagi kalit so‘zlarni belgilang, so‘ng har paragrafning BOSH g‘oyasini toping.
Bitta jumladagi tafsilotga aldanmang — sarlavha butun paragrafni qamrab oladi.
Ortiqcha sarlavhalar bor: ularni chiqarib tashlang.
map: Audioni eshitishdan oldin xaritadagi belgilangan joylar (kirish, lift, yo‘lak) va harflarni ko‘rib chiqing.
Yo‘nalish so‘zlariga e’tibor: opposite, next to, beyond, on the left/right, at the far end.
Hammasi ketma-ket aytiladi — joyni o‘tkazib yuborsangiz, keyingisiga o‘ting.
para: Kalit so‘zlarni sinonim bilan almashtiring, gap tuzilishini ham o‘zgartiring.
Ma’noni buzmang: raqam va faktlar o‘zgarmaydi.
Takrorni oldini oling: bitta so‘zni qayta ishlatmang.
col: So‘zni emas, birikmani yodlang: make a decision, take a risk, pay attention.
Noto‘g‘ri fe’l ko‘pincha o‘zbekcha tarjimadan keladi — ingliz birikmasini eslab qoling.
